version.description: A library to help with any Rust code dealing with poker. This includes card values, suits, hands, hand ranks, 5 card hand strength calculation, 7 card hand strength calulcation, and monte carlo game simulation helpers.
Determine whether characters have the XID_Start or XID_Continue properties according to Unicode Standard Annex #31
A substitute implementation of the compiler's `proc_macro` API to decouple token-based libraries from the procedural macro use case.
Random number generators and other randomness functionality.
Core random number generation traits and tools for implementation.
A small cross-platform library for retrieving random data from system source
UEFI Reference Specification Protocol Constants and Definitions
Raw FFI bindings to platform libraries like libc.

A macro to ergonomically define an item depending on a large number of #[cfg]
parameters. Structured like an if-else chain, the first matching branch is the
item that gets emitted.

The ChaCha20 stream cipher (RFC 8439) implemented in pure Rust using traits
from the RustCrypto `cipher` crate, with optional architecture-specific
hardware acceleration (AVX2, SSE2). Additionally provides the ChaCha8, ChaCha12,
XChaCha20, XChaCha12 and XChaCha8 stream ciphers, and also optional
rand_core-compatible RNGs based on those ciphers.

Lightweight runtime CPU feature detection for aarch64, loongarch64, and x86/x86_64 targets,
with no_std support and support for mobile targets including Android and iOS

build_scripts.rs_poker/5.1.0: Source inspected: std-only table generation into OUT_DIR; no build dependencies or source download/process execution.
build_scripts.getrandom/0.4.3: Source inspected: reads CARGO_CFG_SANITIZE and emits getrandom_msan cfg if needed; no file writes, downloads or processes.

source_inspection_notes.other_new_packages: Published manifests explicitly build=false; no build dependencies.
source_inspection_notes.network_metadata_exception: getrandom package.metadata.cross.target.x86_64-unknown-netbsd.pre-build contains curl and shell file commands for its optional cross-tool NetBSD setup; this is metadata, not Cargo build.rs, not run by ordinary cargo build/clippy/test, and not part of current Windows/Linux workflow.
runtime_notes: Unsafe source exists in RNG/CPU detection/OS FFI; reviewed dispatch and supported-target entry points, not every unsafe operation.
Windows getrandom backend links system bcryptprimitives ProcessPrng through raw-dylib; intended Windows10+; no downloaded DLL.
Linux RNG uses OS getrandom with urandom fallback on supported older kernels.
chacha20 enabled via rand with defaults off and rng enabled, so cipher/zeroize are not in actual root closure; normal CPU feature detection chooses AVX2/SSE2/software implementations.
r-efi target dependency requires target_os=uefi and getrandom_backend=efi_rng; it is locked but not built for ordinary Windows/Linux.
The pure checked poker evaluation path does not call these RNG facilities.
